title: Strict-transform presentations for algebraic-space blowups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $g:Y\to T$ be a morphism, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a quasi-coherent ideal [def-sfb-space-quasi-coherent-ideal], and let $p:B\to T$ be a blowup presentation for $\mathcal I$ [def-sfb-space-blowup-presentation]. A strict-transform presentation consists of an algebraic space $P$ with projections $a:P\to Y$ and $b:P\to B$ forming a cartesian square with $g$ and $p$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], an algebraic space $D$, and a representable closed immersion $i:D\to P$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $J(V)$ for the ideal generated by the image on an etale test $V$ of the canonical tensor map $(pb)^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_P$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Require the kernel of the canonical structure-module map $\mathcal O_P\to i_*\mathcal O_D$ [def-sfb-space-module-structure-map] to be exactly the exceptional-ideal torsion sheaf: for every etale scheme test $V\to P$ and $s\in\mathcal O_P(V)$, its image is zero if and only if there exists a covering sieve $R$ on $V$ such that, for every $W\to V$ in $R$, there is $n\geq0$ for which every further etale test $Z\to W$ and every $r\in J(Z)^n$ satisfy $r\,s|_Z=0$. Thus $D$ is the closed subspace cut out by sections locally killed by a power of the exceptional ideal; its map to the blowup is $bi$. The ideal $\mathcal I$ is retained, so this notion depends on the centre, not just on $p$.
